package_info.package_manager: N/A (Linux malware, not distributed via package manager)
package_info.why_malicious: OrBit is a Linux malware that employs advanced evasion and persistence techniques by injecting a malicious shared object into system processes, hooking critical libc and authentication functions to intercept credentials and log user commands, and establishing covert remote access via SSH backdoors. Its explicit behaviors—unauthorized credential harvesting, command logging, and persistent unauthorized access—are clear indicators of malicious intent.

execution_context.trigger: system boot or user login (when environment variables are loaded)
execution_context.file_location: /lib/liborbit.so (malicious shared object injected via LD_PRELOAD, referenced in /etc/ld.so.preload or set as an environment variable)
required_permissions: network (for later exfiltration and remote access)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At system boot or user login, the malware sets the LD_PRELOAD environment variable to load /lib/liborbit.so, injecting the malicious shared object into all processes, which enables function hooking and sets up the foundation for credential interception and command logging.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Setting LD_PRELOAD globally or for system services to load a non-standard shared object is a well-known rootkit and malware technique for gaining code execution in privileged processes.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate software does not set LD_PRELOAD for system-wide credential interception or persistence; such use is highly atypical and indicative of malicious intent.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Developers may use LD_PRELOAD for debugging or performance profiling in controlled environments, but never for credential interception or persistent system compromise.
key_indicators: LD_PRELOAD set in /etc/ld.so.preload or environment for system services
Presence of suspicious shared objects in /lib or /usr/lib (e.g., liborbit.so)

execution_context.trigger: runtime (when a user authenticates or executes commands in a terminal session)
execution_context.file_location: /lib/liborbit.so (malicious shared object loaded into memory of target processes)
required_permissions: environment_vars (to remain loaded in process context)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Hooked functions: read(), write(), open(), execve(), pam_authenticate()
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the malicious shared object hooks authentication (pam_authenticate) and I/O functions (read, write, open, execve) within system processes, intercepting user credentials and logging TTY commands, then preparing this data for exfiltration to the attacker.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Intercepting authentication and I/O functions at the shared object level is a classic rootkit technique for credential theft and user activity monitoring, especially when performed covertly.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal shared objects do not hook authentication or TTY-related functions for the purpose of exfiltrating sensitive data; such behavior is only seen in malware or advanced security monitoring tools with explicit user consent.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Security auditing or PAM modules may hook similar functions, but always with user/admin awareness and for transparent logging, not covert exfiltration.
key_indicators: Hooks on pam_authenticate(), execve(), read(), write(), open() in non-standard shared objects
Interception and logging of TTY input/output and credential data
Unusual files or logs containing sensitive authentication data

execution_context.trigger: runtime (when an attacker initiates an SSH connection using hardcoded credentials or a hidden user account)
execution_context.file_location: /lib/liborbit.so (malicious shared object persists on disk and in memory, interacts with SSH daemon processes)
required_permissions: network (to accept inbound SSH connections and maintain remote access)
filesystem (to persist shared object and potentially modify SSH configuration)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Backdoor SSH access via hardcoded credentials or hidden user
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the malware enables a backdoor by allowing SSH access using hardcoded credentials or a hidden user account, bypassing normal authentication mechanisms and granting persistent, unauthorized remote access to the attacker.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Implementing a hidden SSH backdoor with hardcoded credentials is a direct and severe violation of system security, providing attackers with persistent, covert access.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate software never creates hidden users or bypasses authentication controls for remote access; such actions are exclusive to malware.
key_indicators: Presence of hardcoded SSH credentials or hidden user accounts in system configuration
SSH authentication bypass logic within non-standard shared objects
Unexplained successful SSH logins from unknown users

attack_chain.action: Malware is deployed and persists by injecting a malicious shared object via LD_PRELOAD, modifying /etc/ld.so.preload or environment variables to ensure system-wide loading.
attack_chain.leads_to: Credential and command interception capabilities are established.

attack_chain.action: Malware hooks authentication and I/O functions within system processes to intercept credentials and log TTY commands, storing or preparing this data for exfiltration.
attack_chain.leads_to: Exfiltration of sensitive data such as credentials and command histories.

attack_chain.action: Malware provides remote SSH access to the attacker by enabling authentication bypass via hardcoded credentials or hidden users, maintaining persistent unauthorized access.
attack_chain.leads_to: Persistent, covert remote access for the attacker.

behavioral_signatures: LD_PRELOAD set globally or for system services, especially referencing non-standard shared objects
Hooking of authentication and I/O functions (e.g., pam_authenticate, execve, read, write, open) in unexpected shared objects
Unexpected logging or storage of TTY commands or credential data in non-standard locations
Unauthorized SSH access, presence of hidden users, or successful logins using hardcoded credentials
file_indicators: /lib/liborbit.so or similarly named suspicious shared objects in system library paths
Persistence mechanisms referencing malicious shared objects in /etc/ld.so.preload or user environment files
Unexplained log files or artifacts containing credential or command data
network_indicators: Outbound SSH connections initiated from unexpected users or processes
Inbound SSH connections using hardcoded credentials or hidden user accounts
Exfiltration of credential or TTY data to external IP addresses not associated with legitimate administration
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for unauthorized modifications to /etc/ld.so.preload and suspicious LD_PRELOAD environment variables, scan for non-standard shared objects in system library paths (e.g., /lib/liborbit.so), detect hooks on authentication and I/O functions within loaded shared objects, audit for unexpected SSH access or hidden users, and monitor for exfiltration of sensitive data over the network to unrecognized external IPs.
